title: The Broken Wolf
premise: Astrid Marchetti, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-hating city of Vell, is given a dying stranger's map to the Hollow Gate — the last door out of Caelwyn, a country erased from every record twenty years ago. Pursued by the Wardens who destroyed her homeland and shadowed by Bren, a disgraced Warden deserter seeking redemption, Astrid follows the map through drowned villages and frozen passes, gathering fellow exiles into a fragile found family. The map's final clue lies in her own suppressed memories: she was the one who sealed the Gate as a child, trading her storm for survival. In the climax at the Gate, Astrid must choose between reopening it to save her people trapped inside the long winter or keeping it shut to protect Vell; she finds a third path, spending her reclaimed storms to hold the door open just long enough for the exiles to pass through, though she herself remains behind. The book ends with Astrid staying in a thawing Caelwyn with Bren, rebuilding what was lost rather than escaping it.
about_author: A. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping coastlines before turning to fiction about places that refuse to stay on maps. They write fantasy rooted in exile, weather, and the families we build when our real ones are taken.

chapters.title: Charms for a Godless City
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. We meet her selling harmless trinkets in Vell, where magic is outlawed, hiding the faint storm still coiled in her bones. A routine day shatters when a bleeding stranger collapses in her stall, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'the Gate' before dying. Emotional beat: the terror of a hidden life cracking open.

chapters.title: The Weight of Wax and Paper
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She tries to destroy the map but cannot; the seal responds to her touch with a flicker of her old power. Wardens sweep the market district asking questions. She recognizes the dead man's face from a memory she buried twenty years ago. Emotional beat: dread hardening into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: A Deserter's Debt
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. A former Warden, haunted by his role in the erasure of Caelwyn, tracks the map to Astrid intending to take it — instead he saves her from a Warden ambush. Neither trusts the other, but flight forces them together. Emotional beat: guilt meeting anger, and neither winning.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Following the map through flooded lowlands, they find a village that officially never existed, inhabited by exiles surviving on smuggled charms. An old woman recognizes Astrid's family name and gives them shelter — and a warning that the Gate demands a price. Emotional beat: first taste of belonging since exile.

chapters.title: What the Winter Keeps
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. The long winter begins early, unnatural and deliberate — the Wardens are freezing the borderlands to trap anyone heading for the Gate. The group shelters in a waystation where Bren confesses what he did during the erasure. Astrid refuses to forgive him. Emotional beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: Three Names on a Map
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Two more exiles join them: Sefa, a child who speaks to snow, and Orla, a healer who lost everyone in the erasure. The group becomes something like a family around a small fire. But Astrid realizes the map's three marked waypoints match memories she has suppressed. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by approaching truth.

chapters.title: The Second Seal
chapters.summary: Bren's POV. At the second waypoint, a ruined watchtower, the seal opens fully and floods Astrid with memory: she was the child who closed the Gate, coerced by her parents to save themselves. She breaks down; the Wardens attack, and Sefa is nearly taken. Emotional beat: identity shattered and regathered under fire.

chapters.title: The Long Climb
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The final ascent through the pass, pursued by Warden commander Ilse Vane, who offers Astrid amnesty if she lets the Gate die forever. Orla falls protecting Sefa and dies believing in the door. Grief-fueled, Astrid claims her storm-calling fully for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into power.

chapters.title: The Hollow Gate
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. At the Gate, Astrid learns those erased were not killed but sealed inside the winter. Vane demands she keep it shut; her mother's voice, preserved in the seal, begs the same. Instead Astrid unbinds her storm, holding the Gate open against the cold while the exiles — and hundreds of the trapped — pour through. Emotional beat: love against duty, paid in full.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Bren's POV, resolution. Spring touches Caelwyn for the first time in twenty years. Astrid, drained of most of her power, chooses to stay and rebuild rather than cross into safety; Bren stays with her, no longer a deserter but a founder. Sefa writes their names into the new maps. Emotional beat: found family choosing home over escape.
